description: CRYPTO_SPEC §4.2: signed statements of variable and environment metadata (Ed25519). var_meta_signed_bytes = LP("<suite>/var-meta-sig", project_id, environment_id, variable_id, name, status, meta_version, prev_meta_sig_hash_hex, author_user_id, chain_head_hash_hex, chain_head_seq); env_meta_signed_bytes = LP("<suite>/env-meta-sig", project_id, environment_id, name, status, meta_version, prev_meta_sig_hash_hex, author_user_id, chain_head_hash_hex, chain_head_seq). The chain and keys reference chain-entries.json's canonical 12-entry chain
binary_encoding: hashes go into LP as lowercase hex strings (the same convention as chain-entries.json's binary_encoding). Numbers (meta_version / chain_head_seq) are decimal-stringified. name is bound byte-exact as UTF-8 bytes (NFC normalization is the signing client's responsibility — §4.2)
chain_reference: chain-entries.json: project_id = the genesis entry hash, chain_head_hash_hex = entries[chain_head_seq - 1].entry_hash_hex, author keys = keys. The canonical chain is 24 entries (2026-09-14 ES + PF1 — the meaning of the positives is unchanged; the negatives gained author-environment-out-of-scope-at-head)
no_epoch_anchor: meta statements carry no epoch anchor (§4.2). Verification rules corresponding to the value signature's epoch-not-current-at-head / environment-not-created-at-head do not exist, and injecting onto a forward meta_version is a known residual undetected by v1 (§14.3-5). var-meta-head-before-env-create being a positive pins this asymmetry
layout_v3: CRYPTO_SPEC §4.2 layout v3 (the schema layout — 0.8-draft session-46 rulings CR / CS for the schema fields and declared; 0.13-draft PF6 R9 for max_age_days): the second valid layout of the variable-meta statement. var_meta_signed_bytes_v3 = LP("<suite>/var-meta-sig-v3", project_id, environment_id, variable_id, name, status, var_type, required, description, max_age_days, meta_version, prev_meta_sig_hash_hex, author_user_id, chain_head_hash_hex, chain_head_seq). The context's layout_version (omitted = 1) corresponds to the wire layoutVersion and selects which layout signed_bytes is recomputed under; the supported set is {1, 3}. status is 3 values (active | deleted | declared — declared is v3-only), var_type is a closed set ("" | string | number | boolean | url), required must be explicit ("true" | "false"), and max_age_days is mandatory: "" (no declaration) or a decimal 1..3650 without leading zeros (advisory like var_type, §14.3-7). The per-variable layout monotonicity: a successor's layout is never lower than its predecessor's (v1 → v3 is the legitimate upgrade; v1 after v3 is layout-regression). Deletion keeps the schema fields verbatim. Environment meta statements stay v1. Existing v1 vectors do not change by one byte (extend by appending — §11)
retired_layout_v2: CRYPTO_SPEC §4.2 (0.15-draft — 2026-10-06): layout v2 (LP("<suite>/var-meta-sig-v2", ...) in retired_var_v2_signed_fields_order — the v3 sequence without max_age_days) is retired and is not a valid layout. Its vectors were removed and the rules they pinned are re-pinned on v3 statements. The negative of kind unsupported-layout (v2-layout-unsupported) is a statement validly signed over the retired encoding that declares layout_version 2: it must be rejected with the typed error UnsupportedMetaLayout before signature verification. A layout beyond the supported set in the other direction (v4+) has no reference statement and stays pinned on the harness side (convention 21's division)

ghost.note: for author-unknown-in-history (a key that exists nowhere in the chain history)

tenure_extension.note: the derived chain for key-from-other-tenure (identical contents to value-signature.json's): after the canonical chain (24 entries), seq 25 re-adds user-member-0002 with new keys (remove → re-add = a different tenure). chain-entries.json itself is unchanged

vectors.name: var-create
vectors.note: variable creation (metaVersion 1, empty prev, status active). The author is the admin at head 12 (member or above)

vectors.name: var-rename
vectors.note: a rename (metaVersion 2). prev = SHA-256 of var-create's signed_bytes (the §4.2 chain)

vectors.name: var-delete
vectors.note: deletion (status deleted, metaVersion 3). name keeps the immediately preceding active name verbatim (§4.2 — do not empty it on delete)

vectors.name: var-nfc-name
vectors.note: a non-ASCII name in NFC canonical form. The signature is bound byte-exact to the UTF-8 bytes of name (§4.2)

vectors.name: env-create-meta
vectors.note: the statement bundled with the environment-creation compound request (metaVersion 1): the declared head is the current head before the append (seq 2 = the create_environment entry's prev — AUTH_SPEC §12-4). The environment does not exist yet at the declared-head time, but meta-statement verification does not check environment existence (§12-4's deliberate asymmetry)

vectors.name: env-rename
vectors.note: an environment rename (metaVersion 2, member or above). prev = SHA-256 of env-create-meta's signed_bytes

vectors.name: removed-author-in-tenure
vectors.note: a past statement inside the membership interval (head 4) by an author removed at seq 5. It verifies under the key of that time even after the removal (§6.3-1 — the counterpart of value-signature's removed-writer-in-tenure)

vectors.name: var-meta-head-before-env-create
vectors.note: positive: a var meta statement is accepted even though its declared head (seq 2) precedes env-prod-0001's create_environment (seq 3). Meta has no epoch anchor and does not check environment existence (deliberately asymmetric to the value signature's §6.3-4 — AUTH_SPEC §12-4; the cost of §14.3-5's known residual)

vectors.name: var-v3-create-expiring
vectors.note: a layout-v3 variable creation declaring max_age_days = 90 (the value should be replaced within 90 days of its push — an advisory declaration like the type, §14.3-7). The domain-separation string is maruhi/v1/var-meta-sig-v3; max_age_days lines up right after description

vectors.name: var-v3-create-no-max-age
vectors.note: a layout-v3 declared creation with max_age_days = "" (no declaration — the empty string is the legitimate 'none' value; the field itself is mandatory in v3)

vectors.name: var-v3-activation
vectors.note: the declared → active transition (activation — a compound with the first value push. The compound's acceptance check is AUTH_SPEC §12-5; this vector pins the single statement's encode / verify and 'activating a declared predecessor is legitimate'). The activation of a v3 variable stays v3 with the schema fields unchanged

vectors.name: var-v3-upgrade-from-v1
vectors.note: a schema reissue that moves a v1 variable (var-nfc-name) to layout v3 (metaVersion 2, prev = the v1 statement) declaring max_age_days = 30 with an untyped form (var_type = "" is a legitimate value of the closed set; description may be empty). Raising the layout is the legitimate direction of §4.2's per-variable monotonicity (a new adoption — AUTH_SPEC §12-11's gate decides its acceptance)

vectors.name: var-v3-delete-keeps-max-age
vectors.note: a layout-v3 deletion (status deleted). Under the same convention as name, the schema fields including max_age_days and the layout are kept verbatim from the preceding statement (§4.2)

vectors.name: listed-author-in-scope
vectors.note: a variable statement on an in-scope environment (env-dev-0002) by a listed author (member listed{dev, stage} at head 19) passes (the permissive side of 3′)

vectors.name: second-device-author-in-scope
vectors.note: a second-device positive: a variable statement on an in-scope environment (env-dev-0002) by allmember-0013's CI box C (cap (member, listed{dev, stage})) passes

rename_fork.note: two valid statements with different contents on the same coordinates (var-api-key-0001 × metaVersion 2). Each branch alone passes all §6.3 checks (both verify successfully); as a pair, the difference in signed_bytes_sha256_hex becomes non-repudiable evidence of server equivocation (§14.2-5 — evidence, not prevention)

branches.name: rename-fork-a
branches.note: metaVersion-2 branch A (signed by the admin)

branches.name: rename-fork-b
branches.note: metaVersion-2 branch B (signed by the owner). Same coordinates and same prev as A but a different name

name_swap.note: swapping the names of 2 variables (DATABASE_URL ↔ DEBUG_ENDPOINT). The 2 proper statements each pass verification, but a byte string with only the name fields swapped fails verification of the original signature (the name ↔ ID correspondence is bound by the signature — §4.2; distributing the relabeled side also fails at the coordinate check §6.3-5)

statements.name: name-swap-var-a
statements.note: the proper side A of name-swap (DATABASE_URL → var-swap-a-0006)

statements.name: name-swap-var-b
statements.note: the proper side B of name-swap (DEBUG_ENDPOINT → var-swap-b-0007)

swapped.name: name-swap-a-to-b
swapped.note: putting var-swap-b-0007's name on var-swap-a-0006's statement fails signature verification

swapped.name: name-swap-b-to-a
swapped.note: putting var-swap-a-0006's name on var-swap-b-0007's statement fails signature verification

negative.name: tampered-signature
negative.note: flipping the last 1 bit of the signature bytes themselves fails verification

negative.name: tampered-status
negative.note: rewriting status (active → deleted) fails verification of the original signature (blocks a signature-free deletion forgery — §4.2's tombstone signing)

negative.name: transplant-project
negative.note: a coordinate transplant to another project fails signature verification

negative.name: transplant-environment
negative.note: a coordinate transplant to another environment fails signature verification

negative.name: transplant-variable
negative.note: a coordinate transplant to another variable fails signature verification (protects against relabeling the value — variable_id binding — to name correspondence)

negative.name: transplant-meta-version
negative.note: a transplant to another metaVersion fails signature verification

negative.name: transplant-signer
negative.note: substituting author_user_id fails verification even under the same key (protects against relabeling attribution — §4.2's user_id burning)

negative.name: wrong-signer-key
negative.note: verification fails under a non-signer key (blocks verification under a different key via FP relabeling)

negative.name: chain-head-swap
negative.note: substituting chain_head_hash_hex (keeping seq) fails signature verification (protects against relabeling the authorization time)

negative.name: chain-head-seq-mismatch
negative.note: substituting chain_head_seq (keeping the hash) fails signature verification (both hash and seq are signed)

negative.name: tampered-prev-hash
negative.note: substituting prev_meta_sig_hash_hex fails verification of the original signature (chain tampering is pinned by the signature)

negative.name: suite-mismatch
negative.note: a different suite means a different domain string, so cross-suite signature transplants fail verification

negative.name: nfc-variant
negative.note: substituting a name signed in NFC canonical form with its NFD variant makes the byte string differ and fails signature verification (the signature is byte-exact — normalization is the signing client's responsibility; the verifier does not normalize. §4.2)

negative.name: env-transplant-environment
negative.note: a coordinate transplant of an environment statement to another environment fails signature verification

negative.name: cross-kind-transplant
negative.note: verifying an environment statement's signature against a variable statement's byte string (var-meta-sig domain) fails (pins the var / env domain separation)

negative.name: head-not-in-chain
negative.note: seq 12 exists in the local view but the hash does not match = hard evidence of a chain fork (equivocation) or forgery — reject immediately (§6.3-2a)

negative.name: head-beyond-local-seq
negative.note: seq 25 is beyond the local view's head (24) = the local chain may merely be stale. Resync first, accept if it matches as an extension, else it is evidence of a fork (§6.3-2b). Pins that the same bounded-resync entry as the value signature is reused

negative.name: author-removed-at-head
negative.note: reject the form where an author removed at seq 5 declares a post-removal head (12) (blocks fresh statements by a removed member's key — §6.3-3)

negative.name: author-role-insufficient
negative.note: at head 6, user-admin-0003 is a reader (the change_role is seq 7). Creating / renaming / deleting a variable needs member-or-above at the declared-head time (§4.2 / §6.3-3)

negative.name: key-from-other-tenure
negative.note: the combination old-key (from the first membership interval) × new-interval head (25) under the user_id that went remove → re-add-with-different-keys (derived chain seq 25) is rejected (§6.3-1's head-time key binding)

negative.name: author-unknown-in-history
negative.note: an author_user_id / key FP pair that exists at no point in the chain history cannot select a verification key and is rejected (the signature itself is valid under this negative's key)

negative.name: v1-nonempty-prev
negative.note: metaVersion 1's prev_meta_sig_hash_hex must be the empty string (§4.2). The form is always checked even by a latest-only verification that keeps no predecessor (the same form as session-14 ruling B)

negative.name: v2-empty-prev
negative.note: metaVersion > 1's prev_meta_sig_hash_hex must be 64-char hex (§4.2)

negative.name: prev-hash-mismatch
negative.note: a chain inconsistency where prev does not match the known previous metaVersion (var-create)'s signed_bytes hash (§6.3-6). The signature is valid — it must not be crushed into an Ed25519 failure

negative.name: revive-after-delete
negative.note: activating after deleted (var-delete, metaVersion 3) is rejected even when the prev chain and signature are valid (§4.2 — the statement-layer counterpart of the no-ID-reuse rule; blocks unauthorized revival of a deleted variable)

negative.name: author-environment-out-of-scope
negative.note: at head 19, user-devmember-0010 is member listed{dev, stage}. A variable statement on out-of-scope env-prod-0001 is rejected by the declared-head-time scope check (3′) even when role is satisfied

negative.name: env-author-environment-out-of-scope
negative.note: an environment meta statement (a rename) is also environment-targeted: a signature on an out-of-scope environment is rejected by 3′

negative.name: author-role-precedes-scope
negative.note: at head 24, user-devmember-0010 is reader listed{dev}. An insufficient-role × out-of-scope compound violation is judged with the role check (3) preceding the scope check (3′)

negative.name: author-device-revoked-at-head
negative.note: a statement by device C — revoked at seq 37 — declaring a post-revocation head (37) is author-key-mismatch-at-head

negative.name: author-device-role-insufficient
negative.note: the effective role of owner-0015's cap-(reader, all) device L is reader. A variable statement (member or above) is rejected

negative.name: author-device-environment-out-of-scope
negative.note: a statement on env-prod-0001 — outside CI box C's effective scope {dev, stage} — is rejected even though the person's scope is all

negative.name: env-author-device-environment-out-of-scope
negative.note: an environment meta statement (a rename) is also judged by the device's effective scope

negative.name: layout-confusion-v3-as-v1
negative.note: recomputing a v3-signed statement (var-v3-create-expiring) with the schema fields dropped under the v1 layout (v1 domain string) fails signature verification (a false layoutVersion declaration v3 → v1 degenerates into a signature mismatch — ruling CR)

negative.name: layout-confusion-v1-as-v3
negative.note: recomputing a v1-signed statement (var-create) padded with empty schema fields under the v3 layout (v3 domain string) fails signature verification (a false layoutVersion declaration v1 → v3 — confusion in the opposite direction degenerates the same way)

negative.name: tampered-var-type
negative.note: rewriting var_type (url → string) fails verification of the original signature (the schema fields are signed — §4.2)

negative.name: tampered-required
negative.note: rewriting required (true → false) fails verification of the original signature (the premise of the presence guarantee §14.2-8 — a required declaration never changes without a signed explicit operation)

negative.name: tampered-description
negative.note: rewriting description fails verification of the original signature (description is also signed byte-exact — §4.2)

negative.name: v3-suite-mismatch
negative.note: a different suite means a different domain string, so a cross-suite signature transplant fails verification under the v3 layout too (the layout version is local to the statement kind and the suite binding is unchanged — §4.2)

negative.name: tampered-max-age-days
negative.note: rewriting max_age_days (90 → 365) fails verification of the original signature (max_age_days is signed byte-exact like the other schema fields — §4.2 layout v3)

negative.name: declared-after-active
negative.note: the form that makes an active predecessor's successor declared is rejected even when the signature and prev chain are valid (§4.2 — no active → declared: do not create a representation that rolls back the existence of a value. Deletion is the only path that removes a value)

negative.name: declared-after-delete
negative.note: a successor to a deleted predecessor is rejected even as declared (§4.2 — 'no re-activation after deleted' also applies to a transition to declared. A tombstone is terminal — pins the scope of the existing reason code revived-after-delete)

negative.name: layout-regression-rename
negative.note: a v1 successor statement (a rename form) to a variable whose immediately preceding statement is v3 is rejected even when the signature and prev chain are valid (§4.2's per-variable layout monotonicity — allowing regression would let one rename silently drop the schema fields, bypassing the presence guarantee §14.2-8 and schema-locked [AUTH_SPEC §12-11])

negative.name: env-status-deleted
negative.note: an environment statement takes only status active (2026-10-07 — CRYPTO_SPEC 0.17-draft §4.2: an environment's deletion is the chain op delete_environment, §6.2, and no statement records it). The former deletion statement (status deleted, metaVersion 3 after env-rename) is a structural violation rejected with InvalidInput — the signature is valid for this byte string; the rejection is not by cryptographic verification

negative.name: v1-declared-status
negative.note: declared does not exist in the v1 layout (§4.2 / ruling CS — protects 'v1 is immutable', the core of the migration). A status vocabulary violation is a structural violation rejected with InvalidInput — the signature is valid for this byte string; the rejection is not by cryptographic verification

negative.name: v3-missing-max-age
negative.note: a layout-3 statement must carry max_age_days explicitly ("" = none; the field is mandatory — fail-closed like v2's required). The bytes are signed as the empty declaration; the context missing the field is a structural violation rejected with InvalidInput

negative.name: v3-max-age-leading-zero
negative.note: max_age_days is a decimal without leading zeros (one value = one byte string — signature uniqueness; §4.2 layout v3). "090" is rejected with InvalidInput

negative.name: v3-max-age-out-of-range
negative.note: max_age_days is at most 3650 (ten years — a longer interval is "no interval"; §4.2 layout v3). 3651 is rejected with InvalidInput

negative.name: v3-empty-required
negative.note: v3's required must be explicit "true" | "false" and does not allow the empty string (§4.2 — fail-closed: do not scatter a default-value interpretation for the omitted case across client implementations). Rejected as a structural violation with InvalidInput

negative.name: v2-layout-unsupported
negative.note: layout v2 is retired (§4.2 — 0.15-draft): a statement declaring layoutVersion 2, signed validly over the former v2 byte layout (maruhi/v1/var-meta-sig-v2 — the v3 field sequence without max_age_days), is refused with the typed 'unsupported layout' error before signature verification (ruling CR's honest failure mode — the signature is valid for this byte string; the rejection is not by cryptographic verification)
